title: Tapping Data Acquisition & Verification — Source Register

sources.title: Drills for use prior to tapping screw threads
sources.subject: Tap-drill (pilot hole) sizing standard
claims_supported: ISO 2306 exists and is a real, published ISO standard
Status: current, not withdrawn, last reviewed/confirmed by ISO in 2022
Scope covers drill sizes for ISO metric threads, ISO inch threads, and pipe threads, for screw threads of normal length of engagement
sources.notes: Direct WebFetch of iso.org returned HTTP 403 (blocks scraping); confirmed via WebSearch aggregation of ISO's own catalogue metadata (iso.org/standard/7135.html title/status) plus corroborating secondary listings (standards.iteh.ai, committee.iso.org). Used only to create the BoltLab standard record's title/scope/status metadata — no copyrighted standard text was read or reproduced.

sources.title: Formula taps into drill sizes
sources.subject: ISO 2306 approximation formula (drill diameter ≈ nominal diameter − pitch) and its resulting ~77% engagement characterization
claims_supported: The 'nominal diameter minus pitch' approximation is attributed to ISO 2306
This approximation yields approximately 77% thread engagement
sources.notes: Secondary trade-press source, not ISO's own published table. Used only to populate a clearly-labeled `derived_candidate` entry (status: derived_candidate, verified: false), not to establish or override any verified hole_preparation value.

sources.title: Ground thread taps for ISO metric threads of tolerances 4H to 8H and 4G to 6G, coarse and fine pitches — Manufacturing tolerances on the threaded portion
sources.subject: Ground thread tap manufacturing tolerance standard
claims_supported: ISO 2857 exists and is a real, published ISO standard
Status: current, not withdrawn, last reviewed/confirmed by ISO in 2022, 2 amendments
Scope concerns the tap tool's own manufacturing tolerances, applicable to short taps per ISO 529 and other ground thread taps of the same diameters/pitches
sources.notes: Same access-method caveat as src_iso_2306 (iso.org direct fetch blocked; confirmed via WebSearch aggregation). No copyrighted text reproduced.

sources.title: ISO 965-1:2026 catalogue listing
sources.subject: ISO 965-1 edition/publication status
sources.notes: Direct WebFetch succeeded on this third-party reseller page (unlike iso.org itself, which returned 403). Cross-corroborated by WebSearch results referencing ISO's own withdrawal/replacement status for the 2013 edition. Used to justify updating the pre-existing `iso_965_1` BoltLab record's `edition`/`standard_status` fields per governance ('correct it only if the primary source confirms the newer edition').

sources.title: Unified Inch Screw Threads (UN, UNR, and UNJ Thread Forms)
sources.subject: Current edition and official title/scope of ASME B1.1
claims_supported: ASME B1.1-2024 is the current edition
Official title explicitly covers UN, UNR, and UNJ thread forms
UNJ (formerly ASME B1.15) was incorporated into B1.1 as of the 2019 edition
sources.notes: Confirmed via WebSearch aggregation of ASME's own published standard record. Used to correct BoltLab's pre-existing `asme_b1_1` record, whose title previously named only 'UN and UNR' — an evidenced, real gap, not a cosmetic change.

sources.title: Taps: Ground Thread with Cut Thread Appendix (Inch and Metric Sizes)
sources.subject: Tap tool nomenclature, styles, dimensions, and tolerances
claims_supported: ASME B94.9-2008 (R2023) is the current edition
Scope covers tap designs/nomenclature/definitions/marking and dimension-tolerance tables
Named styles include straight fluted, spiral fluted, spiral point (with straight flutes / no straight flutes), and thread-forming taps
sources.notes: New standard record created; not previously present in BoltLab's knowledge layer. Directly supports T1's spiral_flute_tap, spiral_point_tap, and forming_tap entity definitions. taper_tap/plug_tap/bottoming_tap/hand_tap were NOT related to this standard, since chamfer-length styles were not explicitly named in the source material reviewed.

sources.organization: Multiple secondary/tertiary machining references (Engineer's Edge, Practical Machinist forum, ToolGrit, 6GTools), citing Machinery's Handbook
sources.title: Thread engagement percentage calculation
sources.subject: General mathematical relationship between drill diameter and thread engagement percentage
claims_supported: % Engagement = (Dmajor − Ddrill) / (1.29904 × P) × 100 (metric form); inch form: ((Dmajor − Ddrill) × TPI ÷ 0.013) × 100
70–77% engagement is commonly cited as a general-purpose practical range

75% is commonly cited as the target basis for standard UNC/UNF tap-drill charts (attributed by several of these sources to ASME B94.9, but this specific attribution was NOT independently confirmed against B94.9's own table content in this phase)
sources.verification_result: formula corroborated across multiple independent secondary sources; specific '75% is the B94.9 basis' claim NOT independently confirmed against a Tier 1 source
sources.notes: No Tier 1 source's actual table content was read. Recorded only as a `derived_candidate` (status: derived_candidate, verified: false) on unc_tapping/unf_tapping — the formula is documented for reference; no target_engagement_percent value was written into any record, and 75% was not asserted as a BoltLab-verified figure.
